item.title: Gotsu Summer Fireworks: Hanabi on the Gonokawa River — Guide
item.description: The Gotsu summer fireworks festival is held on a summer evening over the broad estuary where the Gonokawa river, the longest in the Chugoku region, meets the Sea of Japan at the coastal town of Gotsu. Thousands of shells are launched over the wide water, their reflections doubling the display, in a relaxed local celebration that draws people from across the western Iwami district. Compared with the huge, packed fireworks festivals of the big cities, this is a more intimate riverside affair — food stalls, families in yukata and a small-town summer atmosphere on the banks of a great river.
